title: Portable Trusted Linux
summary: Portable Trusted Linux remains focused on the first Debian Live reference artifact while a first Black Cat application-layer prototype has been added: Black Cat Console. The Console is a mobile-first project/AI controller designed to preserve human-readable project state, improve natural user instructions before AI use, keep secrets server-side, and remain portable to a future local USB runtime. Its source exists in GitHub, but it is not yet claimed as deployed or device-verified.

sections.title: Current focus
sections.content: The core trust-chain engineering focus remains Portable Trusted Linux Prototype 1 and milestone M13. Black Cat Console is an application-layer prototype intended to improve project/AI interaction without replacing the current build milestone. Community Compute Commons remains paused.

sections.title: Core trust chain
sections.content: Authenticated release reference -> verified USB image -> UEFI/Secure Boot -> measured boot and TCG event log -> TPM PCR evidence -> signed UKI -> authenticated dm-verity root -> immutable Linux -> RAM-backed disposable state -> nonce-bound TPM Quote -> independent verifier -> attestation report.

sections.title: Current engineering state
sections.content: The repository has a working direct execution path to the disposable Debian builder through a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner named ptl-builder-01. The declared Debian build dependency set is installed and remotely verified. Manual administrative SSH access has also been recovered and documented. No destructive USB-writing step is enabled.

sections.title: Black Cat Console prototype
sections.content: A mobile-first Console MVP now exists under apps/blackcat-console. It seeds Portable Trusted Linux as the first project, stores durable project cognition in Markdown, accepts text and supported browser speech recognition, provides a Goal/Current State/Constraints/Success coaching step, and can route approved requests to server-side OpenAI API calls when explicitly configured. The source is IMPLEMENTED; deployment, HTTPS operation and iPhone behaviour remain NOT YET VERIFIED.

sections.title: Black Cat local-first direction
sections.content: The chatbot and project controller are treated as interfaces over a common Black Cat Core concept rather than unrelated applications. Remote hosting and remote AI are optional extensions. The intended long-term design allows the same project state and core boundaries to migrate into the local USB environment, with explicit visibility over data sent to remote models.

sections.title: Black Cat remote prototype host
sections.content: The intended remote prototype host is the existing blackcat-chatbot-01 droplet. The Portable Trusted Linux builder remains isolated on ptl-builder-01. No additional droplet is required for this application-layer prototype.

sections.title: Builder administrative access
sections.content: The cPanel host retains the PTL administrative private key at ~/.ssh/ptl_digitalocean; GitHub records only the path, public-key fingerprint and recovery procedure. The known-working bootstrap connection is ssh -i ~/.ssh/ptl_digitalocean root@170.64.224.131. Direct root SSH is transitional and will later be replaced by a dedicated non-root administrative path and stronger credential custody.

sections.title: Verified builder toolchain
sections.content: The post-install preflight detects git, jq, live-build/lb, xorriso, veritysetup, ukify, sbsign, tpm2_getcap, tpm2_pcrread and tpm2_quote. veritysetup resolves to /usr/sbin/veritysetup after the host check was corrected to use a deterministic system PATH. Normal Git checkout and JSON parsing are now working.

sections.title: Pre-build fixes
sections.content: Before the first ISO build, review found and fixed a real path mismatch: the preparation script wrote to work/live-<BUILD_ID> while the build script expected work/live-build. Preparation now uses the stable work/live-build directory and does not require root.

sections.title: Privileged build boundary
sections.content: The GitHub Actions runner remains unprivileged. The next gate is the actual lb build operation, which requires root privileges. Prototype 1 will use a narrowly documented temporary privilege for this build stage, then later replace it with a stronger isolated or root-owned build mechanism.

sections.title: Builder versus attestation target
sections.content: ptl-builder-01 is suitable for build, test and artifact-generation work. It is not a valid platform for claiming successful UEFI measured boot, PCR evidence or TPM Quotes because those interfaces are not exposed. Those gates require a later capable machine.

sections.title: Immediate evidence gate
sections.content: Milestone M12 is complete. M13 remains current: build the first Debian Live reference artifact, calculate its SHA-256 digest and generate the build provenance manifest.

sections.title: Progressive hardening
sections.content: Prototype stages may temporarily use weaker controls to prove the workflow, but every such control must document its trust assumption, compromise path, temporary justification and stronger replacement. The cPanel-held SSH key, direct root administrative login, self-hosted runner and upcoming temporary live-build privilege are bootstrap mechanisms rather than the final trust architecture.

sections.title: Mandatory lessons discipline
sections.content: Every meaningful session updates docs/07-lessons-learned.md and affected specifications or decisions. project_content.json is always written last.

decisions.title: Reuse mature security components
decisions.text: Use Debian, UEFI Secure Boot, systemd UKI, TPM 2.0 and dm-verity rather than inventing replacement primitives.

decisions.title: Independent verification is mandatory
decisions.text: The target computer cannot be the sole authority deciding that its own measurements are trustworthy.

decisions.title: GitHub is the canonical development workspace
decisions.text: Documents, source and the living JSON index are versioned in the private repository.

decisions.title: Lessons learned are mandatory output
decisions.text: Every meaningful engineering/research session records lessons before project_content.json is updated last.

decisions.title: Prototype 1 baseline is Debian 13/trixie amd64
decisions.text: Exact build-host and package versions are captured as provenance.

decisions.title: Community Compute Commons paused
decisions.text: The research remains preserved, but active implementation returns exclusively to the Portable Trusted Linux core trust chain until its initial acceptance gates pass.

decisions.title: Progressive hardening is mandatory
decisions.text: Temporary weaker controls may be used to make demonstrable progress only when their assumptions, weaknesses and stronger replacements are explicit. They must never be presented as final security controls.

decisions.title: Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner is the initial remote execution path
decisions.text: Repository-scoped Actions jobs provide the auditable control path into the disposable build VM. Privileged operations remain explicitly separated from the unprivileged runner.

decisions.title: Build host and attestation target are separate roles
decisions.text: The DigitalOcean VM is used for building and artifact generation. UEFI measured-boot and TPM attestation claims require a separate platform that exposes those interfaces.

decisions.title: Normalize builder capability checks
decisions.text: Host preflight uses a deterministic system PATH so service-account environment differences cannot silently hide installed administrative tools.

decisions.title: Privilege only the live-build construction stage
decisions.text: Live-build preparation is unprivileged. The actual lb build operation is the current explicit privileged boundary and any passwordless permission used for Prototype 1 is temporary, documented and subject to later hardening.

decisions.title: Document credential mapping without storing credentials
decisions.text: GitHub records the builder identity, public-key fingerprint, expected private-key path and recovery procedure, but never private key contents, passphrases, API tokens or recovery codes. Direct root SSH remains a temporary bootstrap control.

decisions.title: Black Cat Console is a Black Cat Core prototype
decisions.text: The chatbot and project controller are interfaces over common project-state, AI-routing, privacy and auditability concepts rather than unrelated side projects.

decisions.title: Project state is local-first and human-readable
decisions.text: Goals, state, plans, decisions, lessons, evidence, backlog and AI rules remain portable Markdown; remote AI is optional and should not become the owner of project memory.

decisions.title: Reuse existing Black Cat server
decisions.text: blackcat-chatbot-01 is the intended remote prototype host for the Console; ptl-builder-01 stays specialised for build work and no additional droplet is needed.

decisions.title: Console deployment claims require real validation
decisions.text: Repository source is not evidence of a working deployment. HTTPS operation, server configuration, API secrecy and phone behaviour must be tested before the Console is described as operational.

changelog.summary: Initial trust chain and threat model.
Established GitHub as canonical workspace and expanded documentation.
Locked Prototype 1 baseline and mandatory lessons-learned process.
Added safe first-stage build tooling and static validation.
Paused Community Compute Commons implementation, restored exclusive focus to core Prototype 1, and added the single-command first real-builder evidence collector.
Provisioned the first remote Debian 13 builder and formalized weak-to-strong progressive hardening as a mandatory project rule.
Established the self-hosted GitHub Actions execution path, completed the first real-builder evidence run, and separated the cloud build-host role from later UEFI/TPM attestation testing.
Verified the installed builder toolchain, fixed the runner PATH false negative and live-build directory mismatch, and advanced to the first ISO build milestone.
Recovered and documented administrative SSH access to ptl-builder-01 using a safe credential-mapping runbook without storing private key material in GitHub.

Added the Black Cat Console MVP source, mobile prompt-coaching flow, project-brain scaffold, deployment/validation guide, static checks and architecture decisions while keeping deployment status explicitly unverified.
